questions.text: A man travels from point A to B at a speed of 30 km/h and returns from B to A at 60 km/h. What is his average speed for the entire journey?
questions.solution: Shortcut: For equal distances, average speed = Harmonic Mean = 2ab/(a+b) = (2×30×60)/(30+60) = 3600/90 = 40 km/h. Full: Let distance = d km. Time for onward = d/30 hr, return = d/60 hr. Total time = d/30 + d/60 = d/20 hr. Total distance = 2d km. Average speed = Total Distance / Total Time = 2d / (d/20) = 40 km/h.

questions.text: What is the unit digit of the expression (7^95 - 3^58)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use cyclicity of unit digits. For 7, cycle is 7,9,3,1 (length 4); 95 mod 4 = 3 → unit digit 3. For 3, cycle is 3,9,7,1 (length 4); 58 mod 4 = 2 → unit digit 9. Subtract: 3 - 9 requires borrow → 13 - 9 = 4. Full: 7^95 = 7^(4×23+3) → unit digit 3. 3^58 = 3^(4×14+2) → unit digit 9. Unit digit of difference = (10+3) - 9 = 4.

questions.text: A shopkeeper marks his goods 40% above the cost price and allows a discount of 15% on the marked price. What is his gain percent?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use successive percentage change formula: \(a + b + \frac{ab}{100}\). Here \(a = +40\) (markup), \(b = -15\) (discount). Effective % = \(40 - 15 + \frac{40 \times (-15)}{100} = 25 - 6 = 19\%\). Full: Let CP = 100. MP = 140. SP = 140 - 15% of 140 = 140 - 21 = 119. Gain = 19. Gain% = 19%.

questions.text: The legs of a right triangle are 6 cm and 8 cm. What is the inradius of the triangle?
questions.solution: Shortcut: For a right triangle, inradius r = (a+b-c)/2. Hypotenuse c=10, so r=(6+8-10)/2=2 cm. Full: Hypotenuse = √(6²+8²)=10. Semiperimeter s=(6+8+10)/2=12. Area = ½×6×8=24. Inradius r = Area/s = 24/12 = 2 cm.

questions.text: A train 150 m long running at 60 km/h crosses another train 200 m long running at 40 km/h in opposite directions. The time taken to cross each other is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Relative speed (opposite) = (60+40) km/h = 100 km/h = 100 × 5/18 = 250/9 m/s. Total distance = 150+200 = 350 m. Time = Distance/Speed = 350 ÷ (250/9) = 350 × 9/250 = 12.6 s. Full: Speed1 = 60×5/18 = 50/3 m/s. Speed2 = 40×5/18 = 100/9 m/s. Relative speed = 50/3 + 100/9 = 250/9 m/s. Time = 350 / (250/9) = 12.6 s.

questions.text: Two circles touch each other externally. The distance between their centres is 13 cm and the sum of their areas is \(97\pi\) cm². What is the radius of the smaller circle?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Let radii be \(r_1, r_2\). \(r_1 + r_2 = 13\) and \(r_1^2 + r_2^2 = 97\). Check integer pairs summing to 13: (4,9) \(\rightarrow 16+81=97\). Smaller radius = 4. Full: \(r_1 + r_2 = 13 \Rightarrow (r_1+r_2)^2 = 169\). \(r_1^2 + r_2^2 + 2r_1r_2 = 169 \Rightarrow 97 + 2r_1r_2 = 169 \Rightarrow r_1r_2 = 36\). Roots of \(x^2 - 13x + 36 = 0\) are 4 and 9. Smaller = 4 cm.

questions.text: From a point P outside a circle of radius 5 cm, the length of the tangent drawn to the circle is 12 cm. Find the distance of P from the centre of the circle.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Tangent radius perpendicular → right triangle with legs 5 and 12, hypotenuse = √(5^2+12^2)=13. Full: OP^2 = r^2 + PT^2 = 25+144=169 → OP=13 cm.

questions.text: A solid metallic sphere of radius 6 cm is melted and recast into a solid right circular cylinder of radius 4 cm. The height of the cylinder is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Volume remains constant. (4/3)πR³ = πr²h → h = (4/3 × 6³) / 4² = (4/3 × 216) / 16 = 288 / 16 = 18 cm. Full: Volume of sphere = (4/3)π(6)³ = 288π cm³. Volume of cylinder = π(4)²h = 16πh cm³. Equating: 16πh = 288π → h = 18 cm.

questions.text: What is the unit digit of \(8^{123} + 9^{456}\)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: The unit digit of powers of 8 repeats every 4 (8,4,2,6); 123 mod 4 = 3 → unit digit 2. For 9, cycle of 2 (9,1); 456 even → unit digit 1. Sum = 3. Full: 8^123 = (8^4)^30 * 8^3 → unit digit 6^30 * 2 = 2; 9^456 = (9^2)^228 → unit digit 1^228 = 1; total unit digit 3.

questions.text: What is the remainder when 3^100 is divided by 7?
questions.solution: Shortcut: The cyclicity of 3^n mod 7 is 6 (remainders: 3, 2, 6, 4, 5, 1). 100 mod 6 = 4, so the 4th remainder in the cycle is 4. Full method: By Fermat's Little Theorem, 3^6 ≡ 1 (mod 7). 3^100 = 3^(6×16+4) = (3^6)^16 × 3^4 ≡ 1^16 × 81 ≡ 4 (mod 7).

questions.text: What is the remainder when 2^100 is divided by 7?
questions.solution: Shortcut: The powers of 2 modulo 7 repeat every 3 because 2^3 = 8 ≡ 1 (mod 7). 100 = 3×33 + 1, so 2^100 ≡ (2^3)^33 × 2 ≡ 1^33 × 2 ≡ 2 (mod 7). Full solution: Compute cycle: 2^1≡2, 2^2≡4, 2^3≡1, then cycle length 3. 100 mod 3 = 1, so remainder = 2^1 mod 7 = 2.

questions.text: If \(\alpha\) and \(\beta\) are the roots of the equation \(x^2 - 6x + 8 = 0\), what is the equation whose roots are \(\alpha^2\) and \(\beta^2\)?
questions.solution: Shortcut: For \(ax^2+bx+c=0\), Sum \(S = -b/a\), Product \(P = c/a\). New Sum = \(S^2 - 2P\), New Product = \(P^2\). Here \(S=6, P=8\). New Sum = \(36 - 16 = 20\). New Product = \(64\). Equation: \(x^2 - 20x + 64 = 0\). Full: Roots of given eq are 2, 4. New roots 4, 16. Sum=20, Product=64. Eq: \(x^2 - 20x + 64 = 0\).

questions.text: If the roots of the equation x² - 7x + 12 = 0 are α and β, find the value of α² + β².
questions.solution: Shortcut: α+β = 7, αβ = 12. Then α²+β² = (α+β)² - 2αβ = 49 - 24 = 25. Full: Roots of x²-7x+12=0 are 3 and 4. Squares are 9 and 16, sum = 25.

questions.text: In triangle ABC, AD is a median of length 12 cm. G is the centroid. The length of AG is:
questions.solution: Shortcut: Centroid divides median in ratio 2:1 from vertex. AG = (2/3) × AD = (2/3) × 12 = 8 cm. Full: By centroid property, AG : GD = 2 : 1. Total parts = 3. AD = 12 cm = 3 parts → 1 part = 4 cm. AG = 2 parts = 8 cm.

questions.text: A shopkeeper offers two successive discounts of 20% and 10% on an article. What is the equivalent single discount percentage?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Equivalent discount = 1 - (0.8 × 0.9) = 0.28 → 28%. Full: After 20% discount price becomes 80% of original; a further 10% discount leaves 90% of 80% = 72% of original, so total discount = 28%.
